ety.text: From Middle English how, hou, hu, hwu, from Old English hū, from Proto-West Germanic *hwō, from Proto-Germanic *hwō (“through what, how”), from the same root as hwæt (“who, what”). /hw/ > /h/ due to wh-cluster reduction in Old English; compare who, which underwent this change later, and thus is spelt wh (Middle English spelling of /hw/) but pronounced /h/ (it previously had a different vowel, hence avoided the spelling and sound change in Old English). Vowel change per Great Vowel Shift.

From Middle English howe, hough, hogh, partly from Old English hōh (“promontory”), and partly from Old Norse haugr (“a how, mound”). Compare Old French höe (“hillock, hill”), from the same Germanic source.
From a Siouan language; compare Lakota háu. Alternatively from Wyandot haau.

senses.d: To what degree or extent.
ex: How often do you practice?
The gauge indicated how hot the oven was.

senses.d: In what manner
By what means.
ex: How do you solve this puzzle? –Sorry, I can't remember how.
How else can we get this finished?

senses.d: With overtones of why, for what reason.
ex: How should I know whether he likes raisins or not? Ask him!

senses.d: In what form, shape, measure, quantity, etc.
ex: How are you fixed for money?
How did you vote in the last election?

senses.d: With what meaning or effect.
ex: How the stock market interprets events has real consequences.

senses.d: By what title or what name.
ex: "How art thou called? Thy name make known; Thy father's name and family,—tell me thy father's and thine own."

senses.d: At what price, for what amount (of money).
ex:
Shal. How a score of ewes now?
Sil. Thereafter as they be: a score of good ewes may be worth ten pounds.

senses.d: In what state or condition.
ex: How are you?
How was your vacation?

senses.d: In the manner in which.
ex: I said it exactly how he said it.

senses.d: Used to state that something is in a certain way or state.
ex: She told me how her father was a doctor.

senses.d: What?, pardon?
The means by which something is accomplished.
ex: I am not interested in the why, but in the how.
It is an a posteriori argument, evincing the fact, but not the how.

senses.d: An artificial barrow or tumulus; in later folklore, associated with fairies.
ex:
Then, the story goes, a certain man
plundered the hoard in that immemorial howe[.]

senses.d: In northern England, a low hill.
A greeting, used in representations of Native American speech.

ety.text: From Middle English however, how-ever, how-evere; equivalent to how + -ever. Compare howsoever.

senses.d: Nevertheless; yet, still; in spite of that.
ex: He told me not to do it. However, I did it anyway. / I did it anyway, however. / I, however, did it anyway.
She wanted to go; however, she decided against it.

senses.d: In contrast.
ex: The conference itself went very well. The party afterwards, however, was a disaster.

senses.d: Regardless of how; no matter how
ex: However clear you think you've been, and however many questions you may've answered, there'll always remain some doubts.
Any rule of thumb, however true (it is), is useless unless you understand its underlying logic.

senses.d: Regardless of how; regardless of the way in which.
ex: Let me know when you've had your interview, however it goes.
However we do this, it isn't going to work.

senses.d: In any way in which; how.
ex: She offered to help however she could.
Wear your hair however you want.

senses.d: In any way that one likes or chooses; in a haphazard or spontaneous way.
ex: I don't care; just do it however.
Nothing was really planned; things just happened however.

senses.d: How ever: an emphatic form of how, used to ask in what manner.
ex: I thought it was impossible. However were you able to do it?

senses.d: In any case, at any rate, at all events.
ex: Our chief end and highest interest is happiness : And this is happiness to be freed from all (if it may) [or] however from the greatest evils.

senses.d: But, yet, though, although.
ex: *She wanted to go, however she decided against it.
